payload.title: Who writes the /goal prompt for a Goal: hyp from the log, or a skill?
payload.body: Issue #113: runs 1 to 6 of checkpoint-store:G-D1CH1R had hand-written /goal prompts. Scenario that separates the rivals: generate the prompt twice from a fixture of checkpoint-store:G-D1CH1R's log cut at the owner answer of 2026-11-11 14:31, and once in a store with a second Goal, then compare the outputs byte for byte and with run 6's prompt clause for clause.

why: Owner question 7 of the grill: a testable choice, recorded as a DesignQuestion.

payload.title: hyp prints it: hyp prompt <G-id> --actor A [--branch B] [--pr N] [--experiments N]
payload.body: A read command derives the prompt from the log: store path, actor, Goal id, the hyp-goal-run skill, the stop clauses and the Goal body's constraints block. hyp-owner-grill's hand-off and hyp-owner-answer's end call it. Same log and flags, same bytes.

why: Rival: the prompt as a derived print.

payload.title: A skill writes it: hyp-owner-grill and hyp-owner-answer compose the prompt from hyp status and hyp show
payload.body: No new command; the agent in the owner session writes the prompt from what hyp prints, as runs 1 to 6 were written.

why: Rival: the prompt as agent-written text.

payload.title: Does the /goal prompt carry the owner's answers?
payload.body: Run 6's prompt opened with the owner's answer it started from. Scenarios that separate the rivals: (S1) hyp-owner-answer records an answer, then its own runner checkpoint, then the prompt is made; (S2) a run writes a refer-only checkpoint after an answer and dies before closing the returned limit; (S3) one answer event settles a key of each of two Goals; (S4) at the 14:31 cut of checkpoint-store:G-D1CH1R, OWED already lists the returned limit checkpoint-store:R-9SMRB2#4 for the runner.

why: Grill round 2 question 2: a testable choice, recorded as a DesignQuestion.

payload.title: No answers clause: the runner reads OWED, which already lists each returned limit and each answered reading to apply
payload.body: The prompt holds no owner answer text and is byte-identical before and after an answer event.

why: Rival: answers stay in the ledger.

payload.title: Answers from state: each returned, unclosed limit and each unapplied answered reading of this Goal
payload.body: Derived per key from the hand moves and applies, filtered by the Goal each key leads to.

why: Rival: answers derived from the current state.

payload.title: Answers by position: the answer events after the Goal's latest runner checkpoint
payload.body: Position-based: the answers recorded since the runner last reported.

why: Rival: answers by position in the log.

payload.title: The owner's scenarios in the grill session decide who writes the prompt
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: the verdict rule is the scenario argued in grill session 285fa63e (2026-11-11). S1: the prompt made twice from the same log and flags must be byte-identical, and made in a two-Goal store must equal the one made from the Goal's own events. S2 (AGENTS.md): a fact detectable from the tree goes into the binary. A rival that cannot guarantee S1 is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from its scenarios.

payload.title: The owner's scenarios in the grill session decide whether the prompt carries answers
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: the verdict rule is Q-MAKJ8R's scenarios S1 to S4, argued in grill session 285fa63e (2026-11-11) from the code. A rival that drops an answer the runner still owes (S1, S2), leaks another Goal's key (S3), or prints what OWED already lists (S4) is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from its scenarios.

payload.observation: S1 and S2 as argued in the session: a read command over the log gives the same bytes for the same log and flags and can refuse a missing heading; agent-written text cannot. The owner chose h-cmd.

why: Session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.

payload.observation: S1 to S4 as argued in the session: position-based answers vanish after hyp-owner-answer's own checkpoint; state-based answers repeat what OWED already lists. The owner chose h-none.

why: Session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.
Owed select, the only candidate; the owner's decision in grill session 285fa63e (2026-11-11).

payload.body: Each candidate is a Hypothesis whose subject is the base plus that commit's change; a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes it. The Goal's lines are its cases.
